Adjuncts and aspiration

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A patient remains obtunded after an overdose. An oropharyngeal airway improves bag-mask ventilation. A trainee says that the adjunct now protects the lungs if the patient vomits. Which correction is most accurate?

  1. Aspiration is impossible whenever chest rise is visible
  2. A preserved pulse eliminates aspiration risk
  3. A nasal airway always provides a complete aspiration barrier
  4. A pharyngeal adjunct helps patency but does not seal the trachea against aspiration
  5. An oral airway provides the same tracheal seal as a cuffed tube
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

A pharyngeal adjunct helps patency but does not seal the trachea against aspiration

Positioning, suction, reassessment and a definitive airway strategy may still be needed.

Understanding the options

A pharyngeal adjunct helps patency but does not seal the trachea against aspiration
Positioning, suction, reassessment and a definitive airway strategy may still be needed.
An oral airway provides the same tracheal seal as a cuffed tube
It sits in the pharynx rather than sealing inside the trachea.
Aspiration is impossible whenever chest rise is visible
Effective ventilation does not prove protection from gastric contents.
A preserved pulse eliminates aspiration risk
Circulatory status does not establish airway protection.
A nasal airway always provides a complete aspiration barrier
A nasal airway also lacks a tracheal seal.
